To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

singular isothermal disks with magnetic fields that are isopedically magnetically neutral (i.e., the magnetic flux density is proportional to the surface density) are dynamically stable, that they can be in unstable mechanical balance at any dimensionless rate of rotation, and that they are not subject to fission into binary and multiple stars at any dimensionless rotational rate.

the fission and fragmentation of singular isothermal disks into multiple bodies is not a viable mechanism for the formation of binaries and multiple stars, and the most promising alternative is that the formation of binary systems is a by-product of the dynamical collapse of magnetized, self-gravitating disks.

(1) nonaxisymmetric configurations exist for all values of the dimensionless rotation parameter, (2) these configurations are unstable to the formation of shock waves, (3) the shock waves are stable against the formation of multiple-lobed configurations, and (4) the nonaxisymmetric bifurcations are stable against the fission of the disk into M = 1, 2, 2,... separate bodies.
